questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city life, the courses at Freie University and the political climate in general.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of guiding from the host university, so it was really good.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of assistance from the Erasmus coordinators upon arrival. They held social events and explained how to apply for courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were a lot of guidance and explanation of the rather complicated and unique semester and course structure. I found it especially helpful to talk to the more senior students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was rather easy because I knew people in Berlin in advance due to its rather close proximity to Copenhagen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That the student housing is quite far from the city life of Berlin and that it at the same time can be pretty hard to find housing on your own due to the 'housing crisis' of Berlin.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't live there, but it was close to campus but far from the city life of Berlin. Therefore I choose to find my own housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was rather easy and explained to us by both the uni and the Erasmus people.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before the stay it went smoothly online. During the stay the Erasmus-people explained everything to us while the professors also tried to help us applying for courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There were Erasmus coordinators and the professors and their teaching assistants who all helped us apply to uni.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I initially got into 2/3 of the courses I wanted, but then I just found some other interesting courses and go into those instead.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to your fellow students and the students who does full master programs at uni - they can help you as they know the system well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved all my courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was very high but the size of the syllabuses were perfect. The seminar based classes forced everyone to be engaged which was really nice.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes were seminar based and the syllabus was much smaller in all of the classes. Bot allowed us to take a deeper dive into the texts instead of prioritizing quantity of pages which tends to be the case at the University of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
30214 Contested Intimacies: Understanding (Non-)Monogamy
29750 Gendered Memories and Resistance: Engaging Women's Quest for Justice through the Museum der Trostfrauen
15481 Ghosts/Haunting theories in the politics of the Middle East/North Africa region
15482 Police and Prison Abolition in the Americas
16093 Democraty and political Meritocracy
16094 Alberto Toscano – Late Fascism

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
15482 Police and Prison Abolition in the Americas - it was so fascinating on racial capitalism and policing and really opened my eyes to new perspectives on police violence and how it serves the racial capitalistic state.

30214 Contested Intimacies: Understanding (Non-)Monogamy - It was so fascinating to reflect on and analyze intimate life, love and relationships structures in an academic context.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy a bike which was rather expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food and groceries were way cheaper than expected. Almost half the price of groceries in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were so much to do and many ways to be social.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could do sports, book clubs, go to parties and just mingle in general at different bars.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to go to the different museums in Berlin as the city has such a diverse and fascinating history.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to potsdam! Its a historical place and makes for a nice saturday trip out of Berlin.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was rather easy as Denmark is not that different from Germany I would say.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You should stay open minded and know that Berlin is a place with so many different nationalities and cultures. therefore its wise to keep and open mind and stay curious to learn more about other people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found the Germans to be extremely fixated on rules compared to danes who are more relaxed about it.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open minded everyone at uni and in the city were towards me as an alien from another country.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take it easy - you will get the courses you wish for. Go out, meet people and stay open minded. Also remember to take a break every once in a while!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Protests in the streets are much more extreme than in Denmark.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in a historical and multicultural metropole while getting to know so many fascinating perspectives academically.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It was tough at times to be away from my family and friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I would really, really recommend going to Freie Universität on exchange. The stay changed my perspectives on the world, Europe and I have made friends for life from all over Europe.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
